paper.title_en: Flavoured jets, vector bosons and quantum mechanics at the ATLAS detector
paper.abstract_en: <p>This thesis addresses three challenges in precision collider physics at the LHC: improving theoretical predictions, extracting particle-level information from data, and developing observables sensitive to previously unexplored properties of the hard scattering. The guiding principle is applying these ideas to processes involving vector bosons and jets.</p><p>A new definition of jet flavour, Interleaved Flavour Neutralisation (IFN), is proposed, and its infrared and collinear safety is tested up to the sixth order in perturbation theory. Alternative definitions of jet flavour are compared to IFN in terms of both their predictions and practical aspects relevant to experimental particle physics, such as computational performance.</p><p>Understanding how heavy-flavour quarks radiate is central to jet flavour physics. A&nbsp;jet substructure measurement using ATLAS data is presented for 𝑏-initiated jets and<br>for jets initiated by light quarks and gluons. The data are unfolded using a machine-learning-based method. The unfolded distributions are broadly described by several<br>event generators, with discrepancies observed in non-perturbative regions of phase space.&nbsp;Unfolded observables can be produced a posteriori using this unbinned measurement,&nbsp;with associated systematic uncertainties.</p><p>Finally, new observables are designed to probe spin entanglement in vector boson +&nbsp;jets processes. In particular, a new Bell-type observable is defined that can act as a marker&nbsp;of spin entanglement for a 𝑊 boson and a gluon. Additionally, this observable provides&nbsp;greater sensitivity to entanglement than previous proposals in the quark-antiquark-initiated&nbsp;𝑍𝑍 production. The potential to exclude restricted families of local hidden-variable models using such measurements is explored, showing that non-trivial families can be&nbsp;excluded using both on-shell 𝑍𝑍 production and 𝐻 &rarr; 𝑍𝑍* decays.</p>
